title: Spacecraft Fire Safety Experiment-I (SAFFIRE-I)
objective_excerpt: (1) determine how rapidly a large scale fire grows in low-gravity and (2) investigate the low-g flammability limits compared to those obtained in NASA's normal gravity material flammability screening test.
approach_excerpt: Condensed from the PSI page: experiment run on the Orbital Science Cygnus resupply vehicle after it departed the ISS; sample was Sibal fabric (75% cotton, 25% fiberglass); air flow velocity 20 cm/s; flame imaged with two cameras; thermocouples, radiometers, pressure/CO2/O2 sensors and anemometers recorded the test.

title: Spacecraft Fire Experiment-II (SAFFIRE-II)
objective_excerpt: The objectives of SAFFIRE-II are to determine how rapidly a large scale fire grows in low-gravity and to investigate the low-g flammability limits compared to those obtained in NASA's normal gravity material flammability screening test.
approach_excerpt: Condensed from the PSI page: follow-on to SAFFIRE-I, run on the Orbital Science Cygnus resupply vehicle after it departed the ISS, with more sample materials (SIBAL, silicone, PMMA variants); the sample card holds 9 samples of 5 cm x 29 cm; air flow of 20 or 30 cm/s, concurrent or opposed depending on the sample; flame imaged with two cameras plus thermocouples, radiometers, pressure/CO2/O2 sensors and anemometers.

title: Spacecraft Fire Experiment-III (SAFFIRE-III)
objective_excerpt: (1) determine how rapidly a large scale fire grows in low-gravity and (2) investigate the low-g flammability limits compared to those obtained in NASA's normal gravity material flammability screening test.
approach_excerpt: Condensed from the PSI page: run on the Orbital Science Cygnus resupply vehicle after it departed the ISS; as a follow-on to SAFFIRE-I it also used SIBAL as the sample material, at a flow velocity of 30 cm/s compared with 20 cm/s in SAFFIRE-I; flow either concurrent or opposed; flame imaged with two cameras plus thermocouples, radiometers, pressure/CO2/O2 sensors and anemometers.
flight_platform: International Space Station (ISS), as listed on the PSI page

title: Advanced Combustion via Microgravity Experiments / Coflow Laminar Diffusion Flame (ACME CLD Flame)
objective_excerpt: Condensed from the PSI page: (A) characterize the behavior of weak coflow diffusion flames of methane and ethylene as a function of velocity and fuel dilution, through measurement of flame shape, lift-off heights, temperatures and extinction limits; (B) characterize the sooting tendencies of diffusion flames with long residence times as a function of velocity and fuel dilution.
approach_excerpt: Condensed from the PSI page: study methane and ethylene diffusion flames over a wide range of test conditions in microgravity; flame chemiluminescence (OH* and CH*) is used to observe lift-off height and flame shape as extinction limits are approached; soot luminosity and laser extinction measure soot temperatures and soot volume fractions; thin-filament pyrometry measures flame temperatures; results are meant to benchmark and improve computational models.
source: NASA PSI investigation page https://psi.nasa.gov/physci/repo/data/investigations/PSI-21 (subresearch area: Flames of gaseous fuel)
